  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Verified from the head view: src/sqllens/safety/rls.py apply_rls (lines 184-318) never folds identifiers. It has no normalize_identifiers call (the base view's normalize_rls_identifiers, base rls.py:184-245, was removed by this PR). It parses with sqlglot.parse(dialect=dialect), runs traverse_scope(tree) (line 239), and decides base table versus CTE reference purely by scope.sources membership (lines 267-291). A table that is not a base-table source goes to reference_ids and gets no predicate. The output is tree.sql(dialect=dialect, normalize_functions=False) (line 318), which does no identifier case rewriting in apply_rls itself. So the 'apply_rls applies no folding' part holds. The base-table versus CTE decision for `WITH "ORDERS" AS (SELECT 1) SELECT * FROM ORDERS` rests on sqlglot's traverse_scope matching the unquoted table name `ORDERS` to the quoted CTE name `"ORDERS"` by exact string. That is third-party library behavior. The item has no `dependency_sources`, sqlglot is not committed in either view, and I did not read any installed copy. I traced the test's assertions (test_rls_views.py:264-267) only as far as apply_rls's own code goes.
